title.en: I'd like to go, I enjoy walking
title.de: Wünsche und Vorlieben: I'd like to, I enjoy walking
title.sl: Želje in všečnost: I'd like to, I enjoy walking
title.it: Desideri e gusti: I'd like to, I enjoy walking

goal.sl: Poveš, kaj hočeš, naravnost in vljudno (I want to go, I'd like to go), nekaj ponudiš (Would you like …?), vljudno prosiš (Could you …?) in poveš, kaj ti je všeč (I enjoy walking).
goal.de: Du sagst direkt und höflich, was du willst (I want to go, I'd like to go), bietest etwas an (Would you like …?), bittest höflich (Could you …?) und sagst, was du gern machst (I enjoy walking).
goal.it: Dici che cosa vuoi, in modo diretto e con garbo (I want to go, I'd like to go), offri qualcosa (Would you like …?), chiedi con garbo (Could you …?) e dici che cosa ti piace fare (I enjoy walking).
goal.en: You can say what you want plainly and politely (I want to go, I'd like to go), offer something (Would you like …?), ask politely (Could you …?), and say what you like doing (I enjoy walking).

say.sl: Kar hočeš, povedano naravnost: **want to** + osnovna oblika. **I want to go home.** (Hočem domov.) **Jack wants to buy a dog.** (Jack hoče kupiti psa.) **Do you want to come?** (Hočeš priti?) Pri he in she je **wants**, **to** pa nikoli ne manjka: **I want to go**, nikoli *I want go*. V govoru slišiš **wanna**: **I wanna go home.**
say.de: Was du willst, geradeheraus: **want to** + Grundform. **I want to go home.** (Ich will nach Hause.) **Jack wants to buy a dog.** (Jack will einen Hund kaufen.) **Do you want to come?** (Willst du mitkommen?) Bei he und she heißt es **wants**, und **to** fehlt nie: **I want to go**, nie *I want go*. Gesprochen hörst du **wanna**: **I wanna go home.**
say.it: Ciò che vuoi, detto in modo diretto: **want to** + la forma base. **I want to go home.** (Voglio andare a casa.) **Jack wants to buy a dog.** (Jack vuole comprare un cane.) **Do you want to come?** (Vuoi venire?) Con he e she è **wants**, e **to** non manca mai: **I want to go**, mai *I want go*. A voce senti **wanna**: **I wanna go home.**
say.en: What you want, said plainly: **want to** + the base form. **I want to go home.** **Jack wants to buy a dog.** **Do you want to come?** With he and she it is **wants**, and **to** is never missing: **I want to go** (never *I want go*). In talk you hear **wanna**: **I wanna go home.**

say.sl: Bolj vljudno, zlasti z ljudmi, ki jih ne poznaš: **would like**, kratko **'d like**, za vse enako. S stvarjo: **I'd like a cup of tea.** ({m:Rad|f:Rada} bi skodelico čaja.) Z glagolom **to** + osnovna oblika: **I'd like to stay.** ({m:Rad|f:Rada} bi {m:ostal|f:ostala}.) Nikoli *I'd like stay*. **She'd like to see the tarn.** (Rada bi videla jezerce.) **We'd like two rooms.** (Radi bi dve sobi.)
say.de: Höflicher, vor allem mit Leuten, die du nicht kennst: **would like**, kurz **'d like**, für alle gleich. Mit einer Sache: **I'd like a cup of tea.** (Ich hätte gern eine Tasse Tee.) Mit einem Verb **to** + Grundform: **I'd like to stay.** (Ich möchte bleiben.) Nie *I'd like stay*. **She'd like to see the tarn.** (Sie möchte den Bergsee sehen.) **We'd like two rooms.** (Wir hätten gern zwei Zimmer.)
say.it: Più gentile, soprattutto con chi non conosci: **would like**, breve **'d like**, uguale per tutti. Con una cosa: **I'd like a cup of tea.** (Vorrei una tazza di tè.) Con un verbo, **to** + la forma base: **I'd like to stay.** (Vorrei restare.) Mai *I'd like stay*. **She'd like to see the tarn.** (Vorrebbe vedere il laghetto.) **We'd like two rooms.** (Vorremmo due camere.)
say.en: More polite, above all with people you don't know: **would like**, short **'d like**, the same for everyone. With a thing: **I'd like a cup of tea.** With a verb, **to** + the base form: **I'd like to stay** (never *I'd like stay*). **She'd like to see the tarn.** **We'd like two rooms.**

say.sl: Ko nekaj ponudiš, vprašaš **Would you like …?** **Would you like a cup of tea?** (Bi skodelico čaja?) **Would you like to sit down?** (Bi se {m:usedel|f:usedla}?) Odgovor: **Yes, please.** (Ja, prosim.) **No, thank you.** (Ne, hvala.) Nikoli *Yes, I like*. Če ti je povabilo všeč: **I'd love to.** (Z veseljem.)
say.de: Wenn du etwas anbietest, fragst du **Would you like …?** **Would you like a cup of tea?** (Möchtest du eine Tasse Tee?) **Would you like to sit down?** (Möchtest du dich setzen?) Die Antwort: **Yes, please.** (Ja, bitte.) **No, thank you.** (Nein, danke.) Nie *Yes, I like*. Wenn es dich freut: **I'd love to.** (Sehr gern.)
say.it: Per offrire qualcosa chiedi **Would you like …?** **Would you like a cup of tea?** (Vuoi una tazza di tè?) **Would you like to sit down?** (Vuoi sederti?) La risposta: **Yes, please.** (Sì, grazie.) **No, thank you.** (No, grazie.) Mai *Yes, I like*. Se ti fa piacere: **I'd love to.** (Volentieri.)
say.en: To offer something, ask **Would you like …?** **Would you like a cup of tea?** **Would you like to sit down?** The answer: **Yes, please** (never *Yes, I like*). **No, thank you.** To something you'd enjoy: **I'd love to.**

say.sl: Vljudna prošnja: **could**, kot že poznaš od can: **Could you pass the salt, please?** (Mi lahko podaš sol, prosim?) **Could I have the bill, please?** (Lahko prosim račun?) **Can I …?** je prav med prijatelji, **could** je mehkejši. Odgovor: **Of course.** (Seveda.) **Sure.** (Ja, seveda.)
say.de: Höflich bitten: **could**, wie du es von can kennst: **Could you pass the salt, please?** (Könntest du mir bitte das Salz geben?) **Could I have the bill, please?** (Könnte ich bitte die Rechnung haben?) **Can I …?** passt unter Freunden, **could** klingt weicher. Die Antwort: **Of course.** (Natürlich.) **Sure.** (Klar.)
say.it: Per chiedere con garbo: **could**, come sai da can: **Could you pass the salt, please?** (Mi passeresti il sale, per favore?) **Could I have the bill, please?** (Potrei avere il conto, per favore?) **Can I …?** va bene tra amici, **could** è più gentile. La risposta: **Of course.** (Certo.) **Sure.** (Ma certo.)
say.en: To ask someone politely, **could**, as you know from can: **Could you pass the salt, please?** **Could I have the bill, please?** **Can I …?** is right among friends; **could** is softer. The answer: **Of course.** **Sure.**

say.sl: Kar ti je všeč na splošno: za **like**, **love**, **enjoy** in **hate** pride oblika na **-ing**: **I like walking.** ({m:Rad|f:Rada} hodim.) **Jack loves working with Meg.** (Jack zelo rad dela z Meg.) **Mrs Birkett enjoys cooking.** (Gospa Birkett uživa v kuhanju.) **I hate getting up early.** (Ne prenesem zgodnjega vstajanja.) Za like, love in hate je prav tudi **to**: **I like to walk.** Za enjoy samo -ing, nikoli *I enjoy to walk*.
say.de: Was dir ganz allgemein gefällt: Nach **like**, **love**, **enjoy** und **hate** kommt die Form auf **-ing**: **I like walking.** (Ich gehe gern zu Fuß.) **Jack loves working with Meg.** (Jack arbeitet sehr gern mit Meg.) **Mrs Birkett enjoys cooking.** (Mrs Birkett kocht gern.) **I hate getting up early.** (Ich hasse es, früh aufzustehen.) Nach like, love und hate passt auch **to**: **I like to walk.** Nach enjoy nur -ing, nie *I enjoy to walk*.
say.it: Ciò che ti piace in generale: dopo **like**, **love**, **enjoy** e **hate** viene la forma in **-ing**: **I like walking.** (Mi piace camminare.) **Jack loves working with Meg.** (A Jack piace molto lavorare con Meg.) **Mrs Birkett enjoys cooking.** (A Mrs Birkett piace cucinare.) **I hate getting up early.** (Odio alzarmi presto.) Dopo like, love e hate va bene anche **to**: **I like to walk.** Dopo enjoy solo -ing, mai *I enjoy to walk*.
say.en: What you like in general takes the **-ing** form after **like**, **love**, **enjoy** and **hate**: **I like walking.** **Jack loves working with Meg.** **Mrs Birkett enjoys cooking.** **I hate getting up early.** After like, love and hate **to** is right too: **I like to walk.** After enjoy only -ing: **I enjoy walking** (never *I enjoy to walk*).

say.sl: **like** je to, kar ti je vedno všeč, **'d like** to, kar bi {m:rad|f:rada} zdaj: **I like tea.** ({m:Rad|f:Rada} imam čaj.) **I'd like a tea.** ({m:Rad|f:Rada} bi čaj.) **Do you like scones?** (So ti sconesi všeč?) sprašuje na splošno, **Would you like a scone?** (Bi scone?) ti ponudi krožnik. **I want** je prav med prijatelji, v gostilni zveni **I'd like** bolje.
say.de: **like** ist, was dir immer gefällt, **'d like**, was du jetzt möchtest: **I like tea.** (Ich mag Tee.) **I'd like a tea.** (Ich hätte gern einen Tee.) **Do you like scones?** (Magst du Scones?) fragt allgemein, **Would you like a scone?** (Möchtest du einen Scone?) hält dir den Teller hin. **I want** passt unter Freunden, im Gasthaus klingt **I'd like** besser.
say.it: **like** è ciò che ti piace sempre, **'d like** ciò che vorresti adesso: **I like tea.** (Mi piace il tè.) **I'd like a tea.** (Vorrei un tè.) **Do you like scones?** (Ti piacciono gli scone?) chiede in generale, **Would you like a scone?** (Vuoi uno scone?) ti offre il piatto. **I want** va bene tra amici, alla locanda **I'd like** suona meglio.
say.en: **like** is what you always like, **'d like** what you would like now: **I like tea.** **I'd like a tea.** **Do you like scones?** asks in general. **Would you like a scone?** holds out the plate. **I want** is right among friends; at the inn **I'd like** sounds better.

exercises.text: — Good evening! ___ you like a table by the fire? — Yes, please. I'd ___ some soup, and my friend would like ___ (try) your ale. — Of course. Do you enjoy ___ (walk)? — Oh yes, we love ___ (be) on the fells. — Mrs Birkett ___ (love) cooking for walkers. Would you like a scone? — No, thank you. ___ we have the bill, please?

translation.sl: — Dober večer! Bi mizo ob ognju? — Ja, prosim. {m:Rad|f:Rada} bi juho, moj prijatelj pa bi rad poskusil vaše pivo. — Seveda. Radi hodite? — O ja, zelo radi smo v hribih. — Gospa Birkett zelo rada kuha za pohodnike. Bi scone? — Ne, hvala. Lahko prosim račun?
translation.de: — Guten Abend! Möchten Sie einen Tisch beim Feuer? — Ja, bitte. Ich hätte gern eine Suppe, und mein Freund möchte Ihr Bier probieren. — Natürlich. Wandern Sie gern? — Oh ja, wir sind sehr gern in den Bergen. — Mrs Birkett kocht sehr gern für Wanderer. Möchten Sie einen Scone? — Nein, danke. Könnten wir bitte die Rechnung haben?
translation.it: — Buonasera! Vorreste un tavolo vicino al fuoco? — Sì, grazie. Io vorrei una zuppa, e il mio amico vorrebbe assaggiare la vostra birra. — Certo. Vi piace camminare? — Oh sì, ci piace molto stare sui monti. — A Mrs Birkett piace molto cucinare per gli escursionisti. Vorreste uno scone? — No, grazie. Potremmo avere il conto, per favore?
translation.en: — Good evening! Would you like a table by the fire? — Yes, please. I'd like some soup, and my friend would like to try your ale. — Of course. Do you enjoy walking? — Oh yes, we love being on the fells. — Mrs Birkett loves cooking for walkers. Would you like a scone? — No, thank you. Could we have the bill, please?
